item.title: Dutch Slope Historic Street — Guide
item.description: Dutch Slope (Oranda-zaka) is a picturesque stone-paved slope in the Minamiyamate hills, in the heart of Nagasaki’s former foreign settlement. After Japan opened to the world in the mid-nineteenth century, Western residents settled on these hillsides — and because locals once called all Westerners ‘Dutch’, the cobbled lanes they walked became known as the Dutch Slopes. Today the gently climbing street is lined with beautifully preserved Western-style wooden houses from the Meiji era, some open as small museums or cafés, their verandas and pale clapboard exteriors giving the area a distinctly nostalgic, half-European atmosphere.
